solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Metal bands stumped by charges

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
raps are criminal charges, as in taking the rap

explanation.surface: Bands of metal on a cricket field are defeated by the bowler's charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Straps can be thin flat strips of metal used to bind or reinforce things.

clue.text: Son covers fruit tree's ooze

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for son sits on top of, so covers, the tree

parts.note: the lime is a tree bearing citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A boy smothers the sticky gunk oozing from a fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is a thick slippery liquid, the sort of matter that oozes.

clue.text: Brought together, the Royal Academy and Liberal fibbed

parts.note: RA is the abbreviation for the Royal Academy of Arts
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics
to fib is to tell a lie, so fibbed is lied

explanation.surface: The art academy and a Liberal politician were united, and told untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallied means assembled or gathered troops or supporters together again.

clue.text: Like the royal spinster without a name? Hilarious!

indicators.note: without tells us a letter standing for name is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: an unmarried princess is prince-less, lacking a prince to wed

explanation.surface: A joke about an unmarried princess with no name, greeted with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal spinster is an unmarried princess, one with no prince: PRINCELESS. Taking away the N for name, signalled by 'without', leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Priceless is informal for extremely funny, as in a priceless moment.

clue.text: Fellow like diminutive Edmund dieted?

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
Ted is a pet form of the name Edmund

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man resembling little Ted has been on a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to go without food, an extreme form of dieting, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Go along with a part of golf course needing a trim

indicators.note: a trim cuts the end off, so the last letter of the golf term is lost

parts.note: the green is the closely mown area around the hole

explanation.surface: Accepting that part of the golf course could do with mowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to concur with someone or consent to a plan.

clue.text: Tons write on the move about time in networker's site

indicators.note: about tells us the rearranged letters go round the letter for time
on the move says the letters of write are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Writing tons while travelling, late for a networking website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the move' turns WRITE into WITER; 'about' puts T for time inside it to give WITTER, after T for tons.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitter was the social networking site for short posts, now renamed X.

clue.text: Unfortunately docks lead stand-offs

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sadly, the dockers' leader brings about standstills in disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a situation where neither side can make progress, a stand-off.

clue.text: Beef cut teacher, say, with learner round at home

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
O is round in shape
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A teacher brings a pupil round to the house for a beef dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirloin is a prime joint cut from the upper loin of beef.

clue.text: Sinatra could be a craftsman of his trade

indicators.note: could be shows the singer's name may become another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra might be thought of as a master craftsman of singing.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker who makes things by hand.

clue.text: Greatest golfer, Ernie, is below standard in matches

indicators.note: in a down clue the golfer's part is written beneath the word for standard

parts.note: par is the standard score on a golf hole
all can mean the greatest possible, as in all sincerity
Ernie Els is a South African major-winning golfer

explanation.surface: The best golfer, Ernie Els, plays under par in his matches.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL for 'greatest' is a stretch, justified by uses like 'in all sincerity', meaning the greatest sincerity.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallels are things that correspond to one another, equivalents or counterparts.

clue.text: Careful reprimand applied to a little food store

indicators.note: applied to sets the scolding word directly against the shop word, the shop first

parts.note: a deli or delicatessen is a small food shop
to berate is to scold or reprimand

explanation.surface: A thorough telling-off is given to a little grocer's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberate describes something done carefully and unhurriedly, with thought.

clue.text: Drink after time — that's a porky pie!

indicators.note: the drink comes after the letter for time

parts.note: ale is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: Claiming to have had a drink after hours is an outright lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky pie' is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, often shortened to 'porky'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale can be a made-up story or falsehood, as in telling tales.

clue.text: Cook a soft sweet

definitions.meaning: to cook the books is to falsify or fiddle them
a soft confection of sugar, butter and milk

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to cook a soft confection.
explanation.definitionFit: To fudge figures is to fiddle them; fudge is also a soft crumbly confection.

clue.text: Company's last word on closure for loft space

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the final letter

parts.note: a firm is a company
amen is the last word of a prayer

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A company has the final say on shutting down an attic space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closure for loft' is the last letter of LOFT, T.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the heavens, the sky or outer space above.

clue.text: Shorten sailor's passage

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, so sailors are ABS
a tract is a passage, as in a digestive tract

explanation.surface: Cutting short a seaman's voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract a text is to summarise or condense it.

clue.text: Manage set flamboyantly for Lady Gaga, say

indicators.note: flamboyantly suggests a showy rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Managing a stage set extravagantly, as a pop diva like Lady Gaga might.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Gaga is the professional name of Stefani Germanotta, an example of a pseudonym used by a performer.

clue.text: Support also floundering for union offer?

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A trade union's offer of backing is also struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floundering' rearranges ALSO to OSAL. The union is marriage, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal of marriage asks someone to enter a union, the question mark marking the twist.

clue.text: Consort let cuff ride up

indicators.note: in a down clue riding up means both words are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
a cuff is a light blow, a rap

explanation.surface: A spouse lets a shirt cuff creep up the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a companion or spouse, a partner.

clue.text: A sailor's westbound with this world record?

indicators.note: in an across clue westward travel means reading right to left

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor sets a world record sailing west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westbound' signals right-to-left reading in an across entry; the world record is a book of maps, not a sporting feat.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of maps, a record of the world's geography.

clue.text: Frothy coffee daughter (European) gulped being a lively girl

indicators.note: gulped means swallowed, so the coffee takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a latte is coffee with frothed milk

explanation.surface: A daughter downs a frothy coffee while being a lively young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladette is a British term for a young woman who behaves in a loud, boisterous way, a female counterpart of a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a boisterous, hard-partying young woman, so a lively girl.

clue.text: Soft song for duet

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A quiet song to be sung by two.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of something, as a duet is two performers.

clue.text: Black tree and dead tree rot

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the alder is a tree of damp ground
the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: A blackened tree and a dead one are rotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is nonsense, and rot is a British word for nonsense.

clue.text: Reward bishop on openings for unrecognised Samaritans

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: openings are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A bishop rewards charity workers whose good deeds go unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Samaritans are a British charity offering a phone line for people in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra payment or reward on top of what is due.

clue.text: Drench a posy of flowers

definitions.meaning: to soak or sprinkle with liquid
a small bunch or sprig of flowers

explanation.surface: Soak a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: To spray is to cover in fine droplets; a spray is also a small bouquet.

clue.text: Shout about men shifting offcut

indicators.note: about places the shout word around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to rant is to shout angrily

indicators.note: shifting means the letters of men move into a new order

explanation.surface: Yelling at workmen moving a leftover piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifting' signals the rearrangement and 'about' the wrapping; offcut here is leftover material, not a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A remnant is a small leftover piece, especially of fabric, like an offcut.

clue.text: Stock holder, perhaps, is beyond help with no head for counting

parts.note: past means beyond, as in walking past

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is taken from the remedy word

parts.note: a cure is a remedy, something that helps

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shareholder is past help, unable to do sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no head for counting' removes C, the first letter of counting, from CURE to leave URE. 'Stock' here is livestock, not shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasture holds grazing livestock, and stock is a term for farm animals.

clue.text: Force husband to be part of faith

indicators.note: being part of means the letter for husband goes inside the faith word

parts.note: trust means faith or belief

explanation.surface: Compelling a husband to join a religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrust is a pushing force, such as an engine's propulsion.

clue.text: Salad veg, in haste it goes off

indicators.note: goes off means leaves, so the word it departs from the haste word

parts.note: celerity means swiftness or haste

explanation.surface: Salad vegetables prepared in a hurry soon spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a crisp-stalked vegetable often eaten raw in salads.
